O.outcome_detail: C3 eye-movement entropy, indexing face-scanning consistency

cells.quote: Among the cognitive ability measures in DalCAB, only the congruency effect in RT of the Flanker task was significantly correlated with C3 entropy, r(290) = .138, p = .018 , padjusted = .036. The congruency effect in RT of the Flanker task explained additional variance in C3 entropy  (β = .159, p = .006, ΔR 2 = .025 ), with age controlled in the first step (F(2, 286) = 8.710, p < .001, Table 1).
cells.note: This was an exploratory correlation and hierarchical regression, not a manipulated treatment comparison. Higher Flanker congruency effects indicate poorer selective attention and inhibitory control and were associated with higher C3 entropy, that is, lower eye-movement consistency.

cells.quote: We found that for d′, the indirect ef fect through C3 entropy was marginally significant (Figure 1D, B = -.005, 95% CI: [ -.0096, -.0010], z = -2.009, p = .0 45, padjusted = .090). The direct effect c′ was also significant (B = -.032, 95% CI: [-.0506, -.0148], z = -3.497, p < .001 ), indicating a partial mediation.
cells.note: The study used continuous age rather than randomized age groups; older age was associated with poorer d′, with C3 entropy as a partial mediator.

result.effect: indirect effect through C3 entropy B = .001, 95% CI [.0003, .0018], z = 2.443, p = .015; direct effect c′ B = .007, 95% CI [.0036, .0101], z = 4.092, p < .001

cells.quote: Similarly, for false alarm rate, both the indirect effect through C3 entropy was significant (Figure 1E, B = .001, 95% CI: [.0003, .0018], z = 2.443, p = .015, padjusted = .030), and the direct effect c′ were significant (B = .007, 95% CI: [.0036, .0101], z = 4. 092, p < .001 ). These results were consistent with the hypothesized mediating role of the decline in eye movement consistency in the relationship between age and face recognition performance, suggest ing declined eye movement consistency as a potential mechanism underlying aging-related decline in face recognition performance.
cells.note: Higher false alarm rate indicates poorer recognition; the positive age-related indirect and direct effects therefore represent worse performance for older participants.
